messages:
maya (eng-platform): noticed something odd on the quota dashboard — when I filter to workspace ws-orion the model list shows models owned by ws-horizon. quick check in console:

maya (eng-platform): curl repro below; note the tenant ids in the response

```
GET /api/v1/models?workspace_id=ws-orion
Headers: x-tenant-context: ws-orion
Response: [{"id":"mdl-777","tenant_id":"ws-orion","name":"summarize-v1"},{"id":"mdl-888","tenant_id":"ws-horizon","name":"partner-demo"}]
```

ryan (eng-api): hmm. is this the console UI combining global/public models with workspace models? we do that intentionally, but it should label them and not mix tenant ids.

maya (eng-platform): it's not just UI labeling — the backend response contains foreign tenant_id values. I saw same on staging and prod.

tina (eng-security): severity: high. any PII or secrets in those model records?

maya (eng-platform): models table columns returned are id,name,tenant_id,visibility,created_by. no secrets. but model names have partner names. legal will want to know exposure.

lucas (eng-sre): rollouts in last 24h: catalog-service v2.5.0 and rollout-service v1.9.0. deploy-bot: catalog-service v2.5.0 -> prod @1742022000 :rocket:

deploy-bot: rollout-service v1.9.0 -> prod @1742021500 :rocket:

ryan (eng-api): looking at our internal catalog API: GET /internal/catalog/models?scope=workspace&workspace_id=ws-orion&include_public=true. The internal param mapping changed recently — we added include_global flag to support admin views. maybe a bug where include_global gets set for normal console calls.

maya (eng-platform): stack trace attached: middleware tenant-mapper returns ['global'] for tokens with x-role:admin in some paths, then catalog interprets that as tenant list and returns union. reproducer with admin token:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -H "x-role: admin" -H "x-tenant-context: ws-orion" "https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/models?workspace_id=ws-orion"
```

ryan (eng-api): ugh. that's the routing policy change I landed to let org admins preview global assets. the intention was to short-circuit when caller_role==admin and set include_global=true, but I forgot to preserve workspace_id when calling catalog for the console path — the catalog call ended up with tenant list = ['global'] only.

tina (eng-security): steps: open incident, rotate any admin tokens? probably not necessary but audit usage. create cross-tenant-read metric and dashboard tile.

lucas (eng-sre): creating an ad-hoc prometheus counter cross_tenant_responses_total when response contains tenant_id != request_tenant. I'll wire it into Grafana and page on rate > 0.

april (product): product impact: if partner names leaked, support/legal need to prepare. april (product) to eli (legal): can you draft a disclosure template?

eli (legal): yes — need list of affected tenants and timeframe. collect from SRE.

ryan (eng-api): immediate mitigation I can ship: change catalog call to always pass explicit workspace_id and use DB filter `WHERE tenant_id = $1 OR visibility='public'` rather than ANY(array). that stops returning arbitrary tenants. will open hotfix PR.

maya (eng-platform): also suggest server-side guard: catalog returns an error if tenant array does not include the requester_tenant unless caller is an internal system user. fewer accidental unions.

ryan (eng-api): debated internally: do we make admin preview an explicit separate API /internal/preview so we avoid widening the contract of /internal/catalog/models? My vote: yes — keep narrow contract and a separate admin-only preview endpoint.

tina (eng-security): agree. plus add an assertion in auth middleware: if x-role==admin then annotate audit header x-admin-preview=true and require special key.

lucas (eng-sre): rollback plan: revert catalog-service v2.5.0 on canary and prod if cross_tenant_responses spike. I'm kicking off rollback to 2.4.3 on canary now.

deploy-bot: rollback catalog-service -> 2.4.3 started @1742023600 :arrow_backward:

maya (eng-platform): I've added an e2e test that uses admin and workspace tokens against the console route to validate tenant scoping. will attach to CI.

april (product): also check dashboards and quotas pages — the quota view was where I first saw the stray model. could be multiple surfaces showing blended data.

ryan (eng-api): good catch. could also affect per-route telemetry that aggregates model usage by tenant if we join on model_id without verifying tenant. will audit telemetry ETL for tenant scoping assumptions.

tina (eng-security): forensics: collect all `catalog.query` logs with response arrays containing tenant_ids not equal to request_tenant for last 14 days. add span ids. create INC-2026-249 and set priority P0.

lucas (eng-sre): dashboards: added a temporary Grafana panel highlighting cross_tenant_responses_total and a top-10 list of foreign tenant_ids observed. paging on >0.

ryan (eng-api): PR opened: hotfix/explicit-tenant-filter. also proposal doc for admin-preview endpoint: /internal/preview/models. tagging for API review.

maya (eng-platform): UX/rollouts note: rollout-service feature flags make it easy to hide the admin-preview from canary. recommend default-off until we have approval and audit. also improve rollout UX: require a confirmation when enabling "broaden tenant scope" flags.

april (product): product will block any release that could surface partner names until legal signs off on disclosure copy.

eli (legal): please dump affected workspace list and timestamps to me as CSV.

tina (eng-security): after hotfix and rollback, run targeted queries to identify any customers who might have seen foreign tenant ids (based on access logs). we'll coordinate disclosure.

lucas (eng-sre): rollback completed on canary @1742023720. monitoring. no new cross-tenant hits so far.

maya (eng-platform): summary action items: 1) merge hotfix explicit tenant filter + e2e tests 2) add server-side guard and middleware assertions 3) create admin-preview separate endpoint and migrate functionality 4) telemetry + Grafana alert + incident runbook 5) legal/customer disclosure work 6) improve rollout UX for flags that alter scoping.

ryan (eng-api): I'll follow up on API doc and a small compatibility note for internal tools.

april (product): thanks team — please keep INC-2026-249 updated.

tina (eng-security): postmortem checklist: root cause (routing policy change + middleware bug), timeline, exposure scope, tests missing, detection gaps, and remediation status.

maya (eng-platform): attaching repro curl and stack traces to the incident channel. keeping this thread as canonical until postmortem complete.
